# Type system overview

Edva is a statically typed, expression-oriented systems programming language. It eliminates implicit conversions, defaults, and runtime reflection overhead:
a value must be typed explicitly by an annotation, a function signature, a literal suffix, or bidirectional constraint unification with surrounding expressions.

At runtime, Edva does not use dynamic type tags, RTTI, or virtual method tables. Function values carry only an unadorned function pointer and closure environment pointer (`{ fn_ptr, env_ptr }`). Data records and containers maintain predictable, C-compatible structural layouts.

## Native type taxonomy

Native type names in Edva are strictly uppercase (`Int`, `Float`, `String`, `Addr`, `Rune`, `Builder`, `Error`, `Type`), complemented by explicit bit-width LLVM scalar types (`i8`--`i64`, `u8`--`u64`, `f32`, `ptr`, `void`) and composite structural shapes.

| Category | Native Type | LLVM / Runtime Representation | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Integers** | [`Int`](int.qmd), `i8`..`i64`, `u8`..`u64` | `i64`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32` | Two's complement signed and unsigned fixed-width integers |
| **Floating-Point** | [`Float`](float.qmd), `f32`, `f64` | `double`, `float` | IEEE 754 single and double precision floating-point numbers |
| **Characters** | [`Rune`](rune.qmd) | `i64` | Unicode scalar value (U+0000 to U+10FFFF) |
| **Byte Strings** | [`String`](string.qmd) | `{ i64 len, ptr data }` | Immutable, length-prefixed, NUL-reserved byte sequence |
| **Buffers** | [`Builder`](builder.qmd) | `{ i64 len, ptr data, i64 cap }` | Uniquely owned, growable mutable byte buffer |
| **Ramifications** | [`Flag` & Rams](ram.qmd) | `i1` or `{ i64 tag, ptr payload }` | Binary polarities, options, fallibles, and results |
| **Records** | [`Record`](record.qmd) | `{ T1, T2, ... }` | Named, positional, homogeneous, and packed bitfield records |
| **Arrays & Slices** | [`Array` & `Slice`](array.qmd) | `{ i64 len, ptr data, i64 cap }` | Growable dynamic arrays and non-owning contiguous slices |
| **Hash Maps** | [`Map`](map.qmd) | `{ ptr table, i64 count, i64 cap }` | Associative key-value tables (`Key ^ Value`) |
| **Addresses** | [`Addr`](addr.qmd) | `ptr` | Raw memory pointers, FFI handles, and system allocations |
| **Functions** | [Functions and closures](functions.qmd) | `{ ptr fn_ptr, ptr env_ptr }` | First-class closures and arrow signatures |
| **Errors** | [`Error`](error.qmd) | `{ i64 code, String msg, String file, i64 line, i64 col }` | Structured error diagnostic records with unwrapping semantics |
| **Metatypes** | [`Type`](type.qmd) | *Compile-time only (erased)* | Compile-time types, `#size`, `#align`, and type generators |
| **Unit** | [`Unit`](unit.qmd) | `void` / empty | Zero-sized value `()` denoting expressions evaluated solely for side effects |

## General type rules

### No implicit coercion
Edva strictly forbids implicit type widening, sign conversion, or integer-to-float promotion. For example, adding an `Int` to a `Float` or passing an `i32` where `Int` (`i64`) is expected produces a compile-time type mismatch error (`E3001`). All conversions must be explicit via constructor invocations (`Int(f)`, `Float(n)`, `i32(x)`).

### Strict initialization
Uninitialized variables cannot be read. While composite values declared with whole-value assignment (`=`) are initialized immediately, forward-annotated records (`r: Record`) are not zero-filled; definite-assignment analysis rejects any path that attempts to read an unwritten field.
